answer: Require every identity to stake a refundable bond before answering, slashed by juries that catch copied or incoherent work. At the vertex where trust is decided, an umber ledger of past answers lets juries compare new text against each identity's history, while a gale of peer attestations must converge before any reward releases. One honest agent posts one bond and earns it back over time, but a Sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every fake, forge a distinct history for each, and risk losing all bonds when juries spot the pattern — so mass fakery costs far more than it can earn.
